stem: When teaching about posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) recognition during evaluation, which systemic symptom aligns with standard presentation references?

options.text: Night sweats never occur with PTLD
PTLD presents only with isolated graft tenderness without systemic symptoms
Night sweats indicate PTLD only when fever is absent

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include night sweats along with fever, lymphadenopathy, weight loss, and mononucleosis-like symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Night sweats are specifically listed among PTLD presentations.
rationale_incorrect.C: PTLD may be asymptomatic or present with systemic symptoms rather than isolated graft tenderness alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Night sweats may occur with or without other systemic findings and warrant evaluation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 6, Noninfectious Diseases → PTLD → 3. Clinical presentation → c.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 6 → PTLD → 3.c. (night sweats among clinical presentations); PDF p. 281 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Night-sweats presentation angle distinct from symptom-cluster item (cctc-2111) and PTLD recognition combo (cctc-2136); anchor verified on Cupples p. 281.

stem: A lung transplant recipient develops persistent cough and upper airway symptoms several months post-transplant. Which PTLD presentation aligns with standard references?

options.text: Upper respiratory infection may be part of PTLD clinical presentation
Upper respiratory symptoms exclude PTLD from the differential
PTLD never involves the respiratory tract
Respiratory symptoms indicate only bacterial pneumonia and never PTLD

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include upper respiratory infection along with pulmonary lesions, fever, lymphadenopathy, and other systemic symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: Upper respiratory infection is listed among PTLD presentations rather than excluding it.
rationale_incorrect.C: Lung lesions and upper respiratory symptoms may occur with PTLD.
rationale_incorrect.D: Respiratory symptoms may reflect PTLD or infection and require clinical evaluation.

stem: An intestinal transplant recipient reports chronic diarrhea and weight loss without fever. Which PTLD presentation aligns with standard references?

options.text: Diarrhea may be part of PTLD clinical presentation
Diarrhea excludes PTLD because PTLD is always asymptomatic
GI symptoms never occur with PTLD
Diarrhea indicates only medication side effects and never PTLD

explanation.rationale_correct: PTLD clinical presentation may include diarrhea and weight loss along with abdominal pain, GI tract involvement, and other systemic symptoms.

rationale_incorrect.B: PTLD may be asymptomatic but can also present with diarrhea and other GI symptoms.
rationale_incorrect.C: GI symptoms including diarrhea and intestinal perforation may occur with PTLD.
rationale_incorrect.D: Chronic diarrhea warrants evaluation for PTLD as well as other causes.

stem: A coordinator is updating PTLD treatment teaching for the evaluation team. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Antiviral therapy is among PTLD treatment options.
Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) is a listed treatment option.
Cytotoxic chemotherapy may be used for PTLD.
Initial PTLD management always requires intensifying all immunosuppression without evaluation.

explanation.rationale_correct: Antiviral therapy, IVIG, and cytotoxic chemotherapy are cited PTLD treatment options. Statement IV is false because reduction or withdrawal of immunosuppression is the initial principle rather than intensifying all immunosuppression.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—cytotoxic chemotherapy is among treatment options.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because immunosuppression is reduced or withdrawn rather than intensified as initial management.
